title: Log power spectrogram
goal:
DS2 feeds the network a spectrogram of power-normalized audio (Section 3.1). Build the feature yourself.

Write `log_power_spectrogram(x, sr, win_ms=20, hop_ms=10, eps=1e-10)`. `x` is a 1-D waveform and `sr` is the sample rate in Hz. Convert the window and hop to samples with `int(round(sr * ms / 1000))`. Cut `x` into frames of `win` samples that start every `hop` samples, with no padding, so there are `1 + (len(x) - win) // hop` frames. Multiply each frame by a symmetric Hann window (`np.hanning(win)`), take the real FFT of exactly `win` points, square the magnitude, add `eps`, and take the natural log.

Return an array of shape `(n_frames, win // 2 + 1)`. Row $k$ is frame $k$ and column $b$ is the frequency $b \cdot sr / win$ Hz.
hints: For 16 kHz audio, 20 ms is 320 samples and 10 ms is 160 samples. One second of audio gives `1 + (16000 - 320) // 160 = 99` frames.
Build the frames with a list comprehension: `x[i * hop : i * hop + win]` for `i` in `range(n_frames)`. Stack them into an `(n_frames, win)` array.
Use `np.fft.rfft(frames * window, axis=1)`. The `axis=1` argument transforms each frame, not each frequency bin.
`np.abs(spec) ** 2` is the power. Add `eps` before the log so that silence gives `log(eps)` and not `-inf`.
Check your work with a 1000 Hz sine at 16 kHz. The bin spacing is 16000 / 320 = 50 Hz, so every frame peaks in bin 20.
